overview: The village associated with the 1286 murder of Eric V of Denmark.

contentSections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Finderup in central Jutland became infamous as the site of the murder of Eric V of Denmark on 22 November 1286. Eric was killed in his bed by noble conspirators, one of the most politically significant assassinations in medieval Danish history.

contentSections.title: Legacy
paragraphs: Eric's murder at Finderup remained officially unsolved, though Marshal Stig Andersen was widely blamed and forced into exile. The killing reflected deep conflict between the Danish crown and the aristocracy over royal authority and noble privilege. The fallout shaped Danish constitutional conflict for a generation.
